vignette: A 41-year-old woman had left pleuritic chest pain and a pleural effusion. Antibiotics eased the first pain, but a similar effusion and pain appeared on the opposite side. ECG, blood gases, echocardiography, and D-dimer were unrevealing. CT pulmonary angiography unexpectedly showed a pulmonary embolus in the right pulmonary artery. She recovered after anticoagulation.

A 40-year-old man with well-controlled HIV developed a month of worsening headaches and then right-sided numbness, weakness, slurred speech, and confusion. Brain imaging showed multifocal acute infarcts. Cerebrospinal fluid had a reactive VDRL. He improved after a 14-day course of penicillin, supporting an infectious vascular cause of his stroke.

A 5-year-old boy had progressive shortness of breath over six months. Evaluation identified pulmonary alveolar proteinosis associated with a previously undescribed CSF2RA gene variant. Whole-lung lavage was followed by meaningful clinical improvement.

A 13-year-old boy developed a progressively enlarging painful posterior cervical swelling over three months. He had marked leukocytosis and anemia, and lymphoma and tuberculosis were initially considered. Excision biopsy showed histiocytes with emperipolesis and diffuse S100 staining, establishing the reported histiocytic disorder.

A patient with recurrent abdominal discomfort and findings of segmental intrahepatic bile-duct dilatation underwent genetic evaluation. Pathogenic PKHD1 variants supported the diagnosis of the congenital biliary disorder described in the report; the syndrome label was used when congenital hepatic fibrosis accompanied the ductal changes.

A 50-day-old boy had persistent loose stools, low-grade fever, vomiting, abdominal bloating, and failure to thrive despite treatment for presumed gastroenteritis and sepsis. Lipid testing and the clinical course led to a presumptive diagnosis of a rare intestinal lipid-transport disorder. Symptoms improved with medium- and short-chain fatty acids.

A 9-month-old boy had poor head control, low activity, delayed motor development, hypertonic limbs, and abnormal thyroid findings. Levothyroxine and rehabilitation had not improved his condition. Whole-exome sequencing identified a truncating SLC16A2 mutation, confirming the X-linked neuroendocrine syndrome described by the authors.

A girl had developmental delay, microcephaly, bilateral cataracts, facial and limb differences, and elevated liver enzymes. Plasma sterol analysis showed elevated lathosterol, and exome sequencing identified a pathogenic SC5D change. The combined biochemical and genetic findings established the cholesterol-biosynthesis disorder.

A man first developed abrupt psychosis and confusion after group A streptococcal infections during adolescence. Over time he had recurrent neuropsychiatric symptoms without a structural explanation, and the report describes an adult presentation of the pediatric autoimmune syndrome associated with streptococcal infection. Treatment included plasma exchange, rituximab, and ceftriaxone.
gold_synonyms: pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorders associated with streptococcal infections

vignette: A 58-year-old man had months of persistent high fever and hip pain followed by a salmon-colored rash, altered mental status, and progressive systemic inflammation. Ferritin was extremely high, autoimmune markers were negative, and biopsy showed inflammatory muscle changes. The authors diagnosed the systemic inflammatory disease and treated him with high-dose corticosteroids.

A 64-year-old woman with heart failure, diabetes, obesity, and renal impairment had lifelong protein aversion and recurrent episodes of vomiting, abdominal pain, lethargy, and confusion. Symptoms improved with protein restriction, nitrogen-scavenger therapy, and L-citrulline. The report identified an adult urea-cycle disorder despite nondiagnostic genetic testing.

A 54-year-old woman developed fever, dyspnea, chest pain, and profound fatigue several weeks after mild COVID-19. She then developed abdominal pain, diarrhea, headache, rash, hypotension, and cardiac involvement while the viral PCR was negative. The report diagnosed the postinfectious adult inflammatory syndrome and described improvement after corticosteroids.

A 32-year-old man developed months of behavioral change followed by mutism, immobility, abnormal posturing, and assisted feeding. Initial concern centered on catatonia. Brain imaging and later evaluation in the setting of AIDS supported a white-matter infection as the cause of the akinetic-mutism presentation.

A previously healthy 23-year-old man had several days of vomiting, diarrhea, dry cough, high fever, and a rash on his hands, feet, and buttocks. Conjunctivitis, myocardial injury, and severe left-ventricular dysfunction followed. SARS-CoV-2 antibody was positive despite negative PCR, and the syndrome resolved with supportive care.
gold_diagnosis: Kawasaki-like multisystem inflammatory syndrome associated with SARS-CoV-2

vignette: A woman in her mid-thirties developed fever, weakness, arthralgia, rash, cough, headache, vomiting, and diarrhea after a recent viral illness, then progressed to shock. Inflammatory markers were raised and SARS-CoV-2 testing supported recent infection. ICU treatment with steroids and immunoglobulin led to recovery.

A 47-year-old woman presented with slurred speech, dizziness, facial droop, and numbness. MRI showed progressive brainstem lesions. Steroids were given for presumed multiple sclerosis, but deterioration and a previously untreated HIV diagnosis prompted repeat cerebrospinal-fluid testing. JC-virus PCR was positive, establishing the reported brainstem infection.

A 53-year-old man developed abrupt chest pain radiating to his back, shortness of breath, facial flushing, rash, diarrhea, and hypotension about an hour after eating tuna. His wife had milder gastrointestinal symptoms after the same meal. The report attributed the cluster and allergy-like findings to histamine-contaminated fish rather than an IgE-mediated allergy.

A 36-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome had persistent thoracic back pain initially attributed to muscle spasm. The pain recurred with nausea and vomiting; serial testing then showed dynamic ECG changes, rising troponin, and regional wall-motion abnormality. Angiography found critical LAD disease and she underwent stenting.

A 54-year-old man with tobacco exposure and reflux had intermittent exertional substernal pain radiating to the arm and jaw. ECG stress testing was indeterminate, while coronary CT angiography and catheterization found extensive multivessel coronary stenosis. He ultimately required coronary artery bypass grafting.

A 57-year-old man had severe epigastric pain radiating around the abdomen to the back with diaphoresis. Initial cardiac and abdominal tests were unrevealing. He then developed leg weakness, hyperreflexia, sensory loss, and urinary retention. Thoracic MRI showed an intramedullary T6 lesion in an anterior spinal artery distribution, and the final diagnosis was spinal cord ischemia.
